observations: Photo 0: A silver laptop is open on a white desk, displaying a Windows 11 default wallpaper. Behind it is a lit sign for 'JAYSMART GLOBAL VENTURES'.

Photo 1: The same laptop is shown from the back, closed, with a small logo on the lid. The logo appears to be three horizontal lines, possibly a brand mark, but not clearly identifiable as HP or any other known brand.
Photo 2: The laptop is shown from a side angle, open, with the screen dark. The keyboard and trackpad are visible. The same 'JAYSMART' sign is in the background.
No visible branding on the laptop body or screen bezel in any photo.
No stickers, labels, or model numbers are visible on the laptop in any photo.
The seller claims it is an 'HP EliteBook 835 G8' with an '11th AMD Ryzen 5 Pro' processor, but no photo shows this text or any hardware details to confirm.

claims.claim: brand name: HP EliteBook 835 G8 notebook PC
claims.evidence: No visible branding or model label in any photo. The logo on the lid (photo 1) does not match HP's known logo.
No internal components or system information visible. Cannot verify processor type or generation from photos alone.

risks.risk: The laptop is not an HP EliteBook 835 G8 as claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the bottom of the laptop showing the model sticker, or a photo of the BIOS screen or system properties showing the model and processor.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic unbranded laptop, which is significantly cheaper than an HP EliteBook 835 G8.

risks.risk: The processor is not an 11th Gen AMD Ryzen 5 Pro, or the laptop is not genuine.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the system information (e.g., Windows 'About' page or CPU-Z) showing the exact processor model and generation.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a laptop with unknown or lower-tier processor, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The laptop has physical damage, screen issues, or non-functional components not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the laptop being turned on, keyboard typing, touchpad use, and screen brightness/contrast, plus a close-up of the screen for dead pixels or cracks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially non-functional or with hidden defects, reducing value.

proof_requests: Photo of the bottom of the laptop showing the model sticker.
Screenshot of the system information (Windows 'About' page or CPU-Z) showing the exact model and processor.
Video showing the laptop turning on, keyboard and touchpad working, and screen display quality.
response.reason: The seller claims a specific brand and model, but no photo shows any branding or model label. The processor claim cannot be verified remotely. Without proof, the item cannot be priced accurately and risks being misidentified or misrepresented.
